body: `intrinsicsize` is now `width` and `height` attributes mapping to `aspect-ratio: auto w / h`.

I used Claude to research the web compat impact with HTTP Archive and by emulating the change in a browser for 200 affected pages.

Out of the 200 sampled pages (mobile root pages from the 2026-09-01 crawl, emulated in headless Chromium 153 at a 360px viewport):

- 1 broke ([doucujte.cz](https://github.com/zcorpan/sizes-compat-3981/blob/main/out/review/067.png))
- 2 got worse ([kral-buch.at](https://github.com/zcorpan/sizes-compat-3981/blob/main/out/review/066.png), [memoiresdeladistribution.fr](https://github.com/zcorpan/sizes-compat-3981/blob/main/out/review/189.png))
- 1 improved ([texelcampings.nl](https://github.com/zcorpan/sizes-compat-3981/blob/main/out/review/040.png))
- 12 changed in a neutral way (the image becomes the size `sizes` asks for)
- 179 had no visible change
- 5 couldn't be assessed (2 failed to load, 3 were blank or covered by a consent dialog)

The sample was 100 pages from the 11,215 the crawl data flagged as likely affected, and 100 from the 62,796 flagged as possibly affected. Extrapolating to all 14,605,919 mobile root pages, that's roughly 0.0008% broken, 0.005% worse, 0.0008% improved, and 0.05% changed in a neutral way. (With only 1 or 2 pages per verdict these are very rough.)

Details: https://github.com/zcorpan/sizes-compat-3981

The page that broke uses `srcset="icon@2x.png 2w" sizes="1px"` to get the effect of `2x`, so the icons become 1×1. 48 mobile root pages do this with a wrong `w`. We could special-case a tiny source size like `1px` to keep the current behavior and avoid regressing those pages. I'm not sure it's worth the extra complexity, though; it's only 48 pages out of the total 14,605,919 mobile root pages (~0.0003%).

Since broken and worse pages together are roughly 0.006%, I think the post-load part of this change should be web compatible enough.
